title: Design System: TalQ
themeNote: TalQ ships four user-selectable themes (Ember, Warm, Vivid, Paper; default Vivid). PainterTheme is the single source of truth; every color is a token resolved from the active theme. Canonical hex below is the Vivid default. No theme uses cool gray.

display.purpose: Inter 600 25px. The welcome greeting, the largest moment. No serif.

title.purpose: Inter 600 15px. Header conversation title, sidebar names.

body.purpose: Inter 400 14px. Message text. The reading tier.

label.purpose: Inter 600 12px. Secondary labels, roles, button text.

caption.purpose: Inter 400 11px. Timestamps, system messages, Mission Control tile keys.

telemetry.purpose: Monospace (Consolas/Cascadia) 11px. Mission Control values, tags, footer. Control-room legibility only, never prose.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Exponential ease-out, no bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, selection, and small state changes.

motion.name: presence-breathe
motion.purpose: The breathing presence dot and the system-status pill. State, not decoration; honors reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single filled control. Reserved for the one primary action on a surface (Send, Enable, Save).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background:#21e3c8; color:#06201c; font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:12px; font-weight:600; border:none; border-radius:8px; padding:8px 18px; cursor:pointer; transition:background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter:brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #21e3c8; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Default Button
components.description: The quiet workhorse button for non-primary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-default { background:#342711; color:#fcf5e7; font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:12px; font-weight:600; border:none; border-radius:8px; padding:8px 16px; cursor:pointer; transition:background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-default:hover { background:#46341d; } .ds-btn-default:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #21e3c8; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive actions. Recessive until hovered, calm clay rather than fire-engine red.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background:transparent; color:#ff9163; font-family:Inter,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:12px; font-weight:600; border:1px solid #5c3a2a; border-radius:8px; padding:8px 14px; cursor:pointer; transition:background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1),border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background:rgba(255,145,99,0.08); border-color:#ff9163; }

components.name: Message Bubble (Other)
components.description: Received message. Topmost tonal-ladder surface, author-color name in group chats.

components.name: Unread Badge
components.description: The clearest instance of the One Signal Rule. Accent pill, ink text.

narrative.overview: TalQ is a quick, quiet, warm room you keep open all day. The surface stays low-contrast and recedes so the conversation is the only thing that asks for attention; interactions feel immediate. Distinctiveness comes from the warm palette and visible craft, never a display typeface or costume; the v0.27.0 editorial/serif direction was tried and rejected as the wrong register for a chat tool. The system runs on a deliberate tension: a quiet surface and confident controls. Color is a four-theme token system (Ember, Warm, Vivid default, Paper), the user's choice, never cool gray. Flat at rest, with a soft accent glow reserved for state. It rejects generic Material/AI-slop, the Nextcloud Talk web UI, the cold-blue category reflex, and the editorial costume.
keyCharacteristics: Warm surfaces tinted toward umber/amber, never neutral or cool gray, in every theme
One saturated accent used sparingly as the single signal
Flat at rest; warm tonal ladder for depth, plus a state-only soft glow
Inter only; type and spacing carry the hierarchy
Calm chrome, confident controls, fast transitions

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent covers at most ~10% of any screen. It marks exactly one meaning: this needs you (unread, active, primary action). If two accent things compete on screen, one is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Gray Rule
rules.body: No neutral or cool gray exists in any of the four themes. Every surface, text, and divider value is tinted warm. A value that reads as gray is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Lever Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built from exactly two levers, size and weight (Inter 400 vs 600). One face only. No italics for hierarchy, no third weight for chrome, no color-as-hierarchy, no serif/display tier.

rules.name: The Scale Honesty Rule
rules.body: A headline needs a real larger size. Do not fake editorial presence by bolding 14px body text.

rules.name: The Flat-But-Stateful Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Forbidden: decorative box-shadow, glassmorphism, blur, gradient text. Permitted: a soft accent glow that encodes state (active/hover/presence/ambient), tasteful, low-opacity, honoring reduced-motion. A glow that is not carrying state is decoration and is forbidden.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: Raise a surface by exactly one step up the warm ladder (primary to sidebar to secondary to surface). Never skip a step or raise by shadow.

dos: Do keep the accent under ~10% of any screen. Its scarcity is the design.
Do resolve every color from the active theme token and tint every neutral warm, in all four themes.
Do build hierarchy from size and weight only, Inter throughout.
Do raise surfaces one step up the warm ladder, never with a shadow.
Do use the soft glow only to encode state, and honor reduced-motion.
Do give every control its full style on the control itself, immune to ancestor stylesheets.
Do keep every theme at WCAG AA contrast and respect user font scaling.
donts: Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere, including Paper's surfaces.
Don't add decorative box-shadow, glassmorphism, blur, or gradient text. A glow that isn't state is decoration.
Don't use a colored side-stripe (border-left/right > 1px) as an accent on rows, bubbles, or callouts.
Don't reintroduce a serif or editorial display tier; the costume was rejected. Distinctiveness is warmth and craft.
Don't drift toward generic Material or AI slop, settle for parity with the Nextcloud Talk web UI, or regress toward the cold-blue category reflex.
Don't fake editorial presence by bolding 14px text in place of a real larger size.
